p: The European power market data landscape is fragmented. Every exchange has its own API, its own data format, its own quirks. The community alternatives (entsoe-py, kipe/nordpool) are volunteer-maintained and frequently break when APIs change.
nexa-marketdata provides a single, well-tested client that handles:
Multiple exchanges through a consistent interface
15-minute MTU data natively (not bolted on as an afterthought)
Rate limiting so you do not get banned from ENTSO-E at 03:00
Caching to avoid redundant API calls
Proper error handling with meaningful exceptions, not silent failures
Type-safe — strict mypy compliance, Pydantic v2 models
No floats for money — all prices and volumes use Decimal

c: pip install nexa-bidkit

p: Building bids for European power auctions is complex. The EUPHEMIA algorithm supports block bids, linked orders, exclusive groups, and merit-order curves, each with specific constraints that vary by exchange. Getting the domain model wrong means rejected bids or, worse, unintended market exposure.
Type-safe bid construction — Pydantic v2 models with strict validation
DataFrame-first API — build price-quantity curves from pandas DataFrames
EUPHEMIA bid types — block bids, linked orders, exclusive groups, merit-order curves
Comprehensive validation — EUPHEMIA compliance checks, data quality rules, temporal constraints
Nord Pool serialisation — convert your order book directly to Nord Pool Auction API payloads
15-minute MTU support — handles both hourly and quarter-hourly market time units
No floats for money — all prices and volumes use Decimal

l: Build a price-quantity curve from a DataFrame

c:
import pandas as pd
from decimal import Decimal
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from nexa_bidkit import (
    CurveType,
    MTUDuration,
    MTUInterval,
    from_dataframe,
)

# Your bid data as a DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "price": [10.5, 25.0, 45.0, 80.0],
    "volume": [50, 100, 75, 25],
})

# Define the MTU (quarter-hourly from 13:00 Oslo time)
mtu = MTUInterval.from_start(
    datetime(2026, 4, 1, 13, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Oslo")),
    MTUDuration.QUARTER_HOURLY
)

# Convert to a validated supply curve
curve = from_dataframe(df, curve_type=CurveType.SUPPLY, mtu=mtu)

print(f"Total volume: {curve.total_volume} MW")
print(f"Price range:  {curve.min_price} - {curve.max_price} EUR/MWh")

from decimal import Decimal
from datetime import datetime
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
from nexa_bidkit import (
    BiddingZone,
    Direction,
    DeliveryPeriod,
    MTUDuration,
    block_bid,
    indivisible_block_bid,
    linked_block_bid,
    exclusive_group,
)

tz = ZoneInfo("Europe/Oslo")

delivery = DeliveryPeriod(
    start=datetime(2026, 4, 1, 10, 0, tzinfo=tz),
    end=datetime(2026, 4, 1, 14, 0, tzinfo=tz),
    duration=MTUDuration.QUARTER_HOURLY,
)

# Block bid — partially fillable (50%+)
peak_bid = block_bid(
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("55.0"),
    volume=Decimal("100"),
    min_acceptance_ratio=Decimal("0.5"),
)

# Indivisible block bid — all-or-nothing
must_run = indivisible_block_bid(
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("25.0"),
    volume=Decimal("50"),
)

# Linked block bid — only accepted if parent is accepted
ramp_up = linked_block_bid(
    parent_bid_id=must_run.bid_id,
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("35.0"),
    volume=Decimal("25"),
)

# Exclusive group — at most one accepted
option_a = block_bid(
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("40.0"),
    volume=Decimal("150"),
)
option_b = block_bid(
    bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO1,
    direction=Direction.SELL,
    delivery_period=delivery,
    price=Decimal("45.0"),
    volume=Decimal("120"),
)
options = exclusive_group([option_a, option_b])

from nexa_bidkit import (
    create_order_book,
    add_bid,
    add_bids,
    get_bids_by_zone,
    count_bids,
    total_volume_by_zone,
    orders_to_dataframe,
    BidStatus,
    update_all_statuses,
)

book = create_order_book()
book = add_bid(book, must_run)
book = add_bids(book, [peak_bid, ramp_up, options])

volumes = total_volume_by_zone(book)
print(f"NO1 total volume: {volumes[BiddingZone.NO1]} MW")

# Export to pandas for analysis or audit
df = orders_to_dataframe(book)

from nexa_bidkit import (
    validate_bid,
    validate_bids,
    validate_order_book_for_submission,
    get_validation_summary,
    EuphemiaValidationError,
)

# Validate a single bid
try:
    validate_bid(peak_bid)
except EuphemiaValidationError as e:
    print(f"EUPHEMIA compliance error: {e}")

# Batch validation — collects all errors
results = validate_bids([must_run, peak_bid, ramp_up])
summary = get_validation_summary(results)
print(f"Pass rate: {summary['pass_rate']:.1f}%")

# Full submission check including gate closure
gate_closure = datetime(2026, 3, 31, 12, 0, tzinfo=ZoneInfo("Europe/Oslo"))
validate_order_book_for_submission(book, gate_closure_time=gate_closure)

from nexa_bidkit.nordpool import order_book_to_nord_pool

# Supply a resolver that maps (MTUInterval, BiddingZone) → Nord Pool contract ID.
# Populate this from Nord Pool's products API at runtime.
def resolve_contract(mtu, zone):
    return f"{zone.value}-{mtu.start.hour}"

submission = order_book_to_nord_pool(
    book,
    auction_id="DA-2026-04-01",
    portfolio="my-portfolio",
    contract_id_resolver=resolve_contract,
)

print(f"Curve orders:        {len(submission.curve_orders)}")
print(f"Block orders:        {len(submission.block_orders)}")
print(f"Linked block orders: {len(submission.linked_block_orders)}")
print(f"Exclusive groups:    {len(submission.exclusive_group_orders)}")

# Serialise to JSON for the Nord Pool API (uses camelCase aliases)
payload = submission.curve_orders[0].model_dump(by_alias=True)

Python library for building and submitting mFRR energy activation market bids to Nordic TSOs.

Python library for building, validating, and serialising mFRR energy activation market (EAM) bids for the four Nordic TSOs: Statnett (Norway), Fingrid (Finland), Energinet (Denmark), and Svenska kraftnat (Sweden).

c: pip install nexa-mfrr-nordic-eam
pip install nexa-mfrr-nordic-eam[pandas]

p: The Nordic mFRR energy activation market went live on 4 March 2025 as part of the Nordic Balancing Model (NBM). BSPs (Balancing Service Providers) submit bids to their connecting TSO via CIM XML documents over ECP/EDX.
This library handles the BSP side of that workflow:
Build simple bids — divisible and indivisible bids with full attribute support
Complex bid groups — ExclusiveGroup, MultipartGroup, InclusiveGroup with group-level validation
Technically linked bids — TechnicalLink builder prevents double-activation across consecutive MTUs
Conditionally linked bids — adjust availability in QH0 based on activation outcome in QH-1 or QH-2
TSO configuration — Statnett (NO), Svenska kraftnat (SE), and Energinet (DK) fully configured
Validate before you send — common and TSO-configurable rules, pre-MARI and post-MARI price limits
Serialise to CIM XML — generates compliant ReserveBid_MarketDocument XML per the NBM schema
Timing helpers — gate closure calculations, MTU boundaries, DST handling, MARI vs pre-MARI timing
What it does not do: manage your ECP/EDX endpoint. That is infrastructure you deploy and operate separately. This library generates the XML documents you send through your endpoint.

l: Submit a simple divisible bid to Statnett

c:
from nexa_mfrr_eam import (
    Bid, BidDocument, BiddingZone, Direction,
    MarketProductType, TSO, MARIMode,
)

# Build a 50 MW up-regulation bid
bid = (
    Bid.up(volume_mw=50, price_eur=85.50)
    .divisible(min_volume_mw=10)
    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:00Z")
    .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")
    .product_type(MarketProductType.SCHEDULED_AND_DIRECT)
    .build()
)

# Wrap in a document and target Statnett
doc = (
    BidDocument(tso=TSO.STATNETT)
    .sender(party_id="9999909919920", coding_scheme="A10")
    .add_bid(bid)
    .build()
)

# Validate against Statnett-specific rules
errors = doc.validate(mari_mode=MARIMode.PRE_MARI)
if errors:
    for e in errors:
        print(f"  {e}")
else:
    xml_bytes = doc.to_xml()
    # Send xml_bytes via your ECP endpoint to Statnett

l: Build a multipart bid (multiple price levels, same MTU)
p: If the highest-priced component is accepted, all cheaper components are also accepted. All components must have different prices.

c:
from nexa_mfrr_eam import MultipartGroup, BiddingZone, Direction, MarketProductType

group = (
    MultipartGroup(bidding_zone=BiddingZone.NO2)
    .direction(Direction.UP)
    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:00Z")
    .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")
    .add_component(volume_mw=20, price_eur=50.00)
    .add_component(volume_mw=15, price_eur=75.00)
    .add_component(volume_mw=10, price_eur=120.00)
    .build()
)

l: Build technically linked bids across MTUs
p: Technical linking prevents double-activation when a bid in one MTU is activated via direct activation and the resource is still ramping during the next MTU.

c:
from nexa_mfrr_eam import TechnicalLink, BiddingZone, Direction, MarketProductType

link = (
    TechnicalLink(bidding_zone=BiddingZone.SE3)
    .resource("REG-OBJ-SE-001", coding_scheme="A01")
    .add_mtu(
        mtu="2026-03-21T10:00Z",
        direction=Direction.UP,
        volume_mw=25,
        price_eur=90.00,
        product_type=MarketProductType.SCHEDULED_AND_DIRECT,
    )
    .add_mtu(
        mtu="2026-03-21T10:15Z",
        direction=Direction.UP,
        volume_mw=25,
        price_eur=90.00,
        product_type=MarketProductType.SCHEDULED_AND_DIRECT,
    )
    .build()
)

p: Conditional linking adjusts availability in QH0 based on what happened in QH-1 or QH-2.

c:
from nexa_mfrr_eam import Bid, ConditionalStatus, BiddingZone

# QH-1 bid
bid_qh_minus_1 = (
    Bid.up(volume_mw=30, price_eur=70.00)
    .divisible(min_volume_mw=5)
    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:15Z")
    .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")
    .build()
)

# QH0 bid: unavailable if QH-1 was activated
bid_qh_0 = (
    Bid.up(volume_mw=30, price_eur=70.00)
    .divisible(min_volume_mw=5)
    .for_mtu("2026-03-21T10:30Z")
    .resource("NOKG90901", coding_scheme="NNO")
    .conditionally_available()
    .link_to(bid_qh_minus_1, status=ConditionalStatus.NOT_AVAILABLE_IF_ACTIVATED)
    .build()
)

p: The mFRR EAM operates on 15-minute Market Time Units (MTUs). There are 96 MTUs per day. BSPs submit bids to their connecting TSO; the TSO forwards them to the Activation Optimisation Function (AOF), which selects bids for activation.
BSP GCT: QH-45 (45 minutes before the quarter-hour)

The library supports both pre-MARI and post-MARI timing configurations via MARIMode.PRE_MARI and MARIMode.POST_MARI. Pre-MARI price limits are -10,000 to +10,000 EUR/MWh; post-MARI will be -15,000 to +15,000 EUR/MWh.
